minutes.headline: Board voted to send the Hickory Hills kayak-rack zone-one violation dispute to legal counsel, KP Law
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District commissioners spent most of the meeting on the long-running dispute over kayak racks stored inside the Hickory Hills wellhead zone one protection area, ultimately voting to install a gated barrier to block vehicle access and to refer the underlying violation to KP Law after commissioners could not agree on seeking a DEP variance instead. The board also reviewed a new sanitary survey, heard a detailed PFAS well-pumping remediation proposal aimed at avoiding a treatment plant, voted to abandon a planned switch to new billing software, and took public comment on PFAS costs and the kayak issue.

what_happened.line: Commissioners voted to refer the Hickory Hills kayak-rack dispute inside the wellhead protection zone to the district's legal counsel.
The board also voted to install a gated barrier with boulders to block vehicle access into that same protection zone.
Commissioners voted to abandon a planned switch to new billing software and stay with the current vendor.
The district outlined a pilot of running two wells at set rates to try to hold PFAS levels down without building a treatment plant.
A new state sanitary survey flagged manganese, redundancy, and iron/PFAS concerns at district wells.

why_it_matters: The wellhead protection dispute and its referral to legal counsel touches the safety of the water supply and could add legal costs the district ultimately passes through in water rates.
The PFAS well-pumping pilot is being pursued specifically as an alternative to a treatment plant, which affects how much and how soon a large capital cost lands on ratepayers.
The decision to stay with the current billing vendor affects how and when residents pay their water bills, including features like paperless billing.
watch_next: The superintendent's gate/boulder design, to be brought back to the board before installation.
A forthcoming staff report on the costs and benefits of commercial/bulk water sales.
